Date: 2026-07-15
Start: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Aaron Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Ramos (Nyx, Head of AI), Evan Zhao (Nyx, Platform Engineer), Liam O'Connor (Nyx, CTO)
Recording: yes
summary: Discovery focused on model selection for Nyx Robotics' multi-lingual autonomous support agent. Discussed context window needs (up to 8k), tool-calling for telemetry and rubric-based actions, hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs, encryption/KMS and SOC2 questions. Agreed to run benchmarks and share security docs.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, this is Aaron our SE. How's it going?
[00:08] Sofia Ramos: Hi Maya, hi Aaron. Good thanks. We're excited, we put this meeting on to figure out which models make sense for our in-car support agent.
[00:18] Aaron Patel: Great. Quick agenda: understand your stack and constraints, how long conversations need to be, languages, and what tool-calling you need. Then we'll talk hosting options and next steps. Sound ok?
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Yes, that works. I'll be mostly high-level but Evan will answer infra questions.
[00:36] Evan Zhao: Yep.
[00:39] Maya Chen: To start, Sofia, what's the primary user workflow? You mentioned in the docs a support assistant that ingests logs and interacts with the car telemetry?
[00:48] Sofia Ramos: Exactly, so the agent will get a chunk of vehicle telemetry, some recent sensor logs, and previous chat history. Typical convo is 6-10 exchanges but we need the model to see roughly the last 5-10k tokens, sometimes more if we include full session logs.
[01:05] Aaron Patel: So you're aiming for about 8k context as a baseline?
[01:09] Sofia Ramos: Yeah 8k is baseline, ideally 12-16k in a handful of cases when we dump more logs.
[01:16] Maya Chen: Good to know. For model families, are you leaning toward open-source variants or managed like Anthropic/OpenAI?
[01:24] Sofia Ramos: We're trying to avoid vendor lock-in; open models are preferred if performance and latency are acceptable. Cost is a big factor — we have high token volume.
[01:33] Liam O'Connor: Also security/regulatory — some of the data is PII-ish and EU customers want data residency controls.
[01:40] Aaron Patel: Understood. On open models, within Redwood we typically recommend a few paths: optimized open LLMs with 8k/16k context—some are quantized for cost-efficiency—or our hosted managed models. For strict latency requirements, Dedicated pools reduce jitter and give predictable throughput.
[01:58] Evan Zhao: What about tool-calling? We need the model to call internal APIs to pull live telemetry, run diagnostic routines, and trigger actions. Do you support function calling?
[02:08] Aaron Patel: Yes, we have structured tool/function calling. You can register a set of allowed functions, and the runtime will enforce routing and auditing so calls are logged for compliance. There are some caveats with streaming responses and tool-call latency, but we can show examples.
[02:25] Sofia Ramos: Are those calls happening inside the same inference request or as follow-up? We need atomicity for some commands.
[02:32] Maya Chen: You can do synchronous function calls where the model returns a structured output invoking a function and Redwood will optionally call the function or pass the payload back to your infra. For audit we log the returns. If you need side-effects performed inline we can show recommended patterns.
[02:48] Evan Zhao: Ok. On infra, for Dedicated vs Private: Nyx prefers VPC/VPN to keep telemetry inside our cloud. We might need full private deployment for EU data.
[02:58] Aaron Patel: That's doable. Redwood Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem. Dedicated is a reserved capacity in our clouds but with VPC peering options and stronger isolation. For strict data residency and air-gap we recommend Private.
[03:13] Liam O'Connor: Cost delta?
[03:15] Maya Chen: Private has a platform licensing component and professional services upfront; Dedicated is monthly committed capacity. We'll send a cost comparison.
[03:23] Sofia Ramos: SLA — latency targets for tail percentiles are important. We get upset customers if the assistant takes >800ms on median for simple queries.
[03:31] Aaron Patel: We can target sub-200ms token generation on optimized kernels with Dedicated and carefully selected models; hosted latencies vary but have strong SLAs for higher tiers. We'll surface sample p50/p95 numbers for model variants.
[03:46] Evan Zhao: For model accuracy multilingual: we need English, Spanish, German, Japanese — low hallucination on instructions and ability to follow tool schemas. Any recommendations?
[03:56] Maya Chen: For multilingual, some of the larger open models do better, but cost goes up. There's a trade-off: smaller quantized models with adapter-tuning can hit cost targets but might miss on rare-language quality. We suggest running a short eval on your language prompts.
[04:13] Sofia Ramos: We'll provide translation examples and a few prompt templates.
[04:17] Aaron Patel: Perfect. Also, when you say low hallucination, are you doing deterministic checks or human-in-the-loop verification?
[04:25] Sofia Ramos: For high-risk actions we'll always require an approval step. For diagnostic answers we want minimal hallucination — ideally citations to logs or deterministic outputs.
[04:34] Maya Chen: Redwood supports structured outputs for citations and we can plug in retrieval augmentation from your logs. If you do RAG, there are clear guidance and builtin caching.
[04:44] Liam O'Connor: Speaking of logs, KMS and encryption at rest — we need BYOK.
[04:50] Aaron Patel: Yes, Redwood Private and Dedicated support customer KMS/HSM integrations for key management and we keep audit logs. We'll attach the security architecture doc.
[04:59] Evan Zhao: Any red flags around model quantization and K/V cache integrity? We worry about state corruption with quantized kernels.
[05:07] Aaron Patel: Good question. Our runtime has tested quantization profiles and KV cache management; there are known trade-offs with extreme quantization and very long context windows. We recommend our validated quantization profiles for production. We'll run your workload to validate.
[05:22] Sofia Ramos: Benchmarks — we want end-to-end benchmarks including telemetry fetch + model inference + function call loop. Can Redwood run that?
[05:30] Maya Chen: Yes, we can run a benchmark using your dataset. Typical approach: we spin up a dedicated pilot with reserved GPUs, run 48-hour continuous traffic, and report latency, cost per million tokens, and error rates. Aaron will coordinate.
[05:44] Aaron Patel: We'll need sample payloads, your expected qps, and any multi-region requirements. Also confirm whether we should simulate failovers.
[05:52] Evan Zhao: QPS target is around 20 concurrent agents per region during peak.
[05:57] Maya Chen: Noted. For compatibility with existing infra, do you have SSO/SAML and enterprise roles?
[06:03] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Okta SAML and RBAC.
[06:07] Aaron Patel: We support Okta and SAML, and have fine-grained RBAC with token-level auditing.
[06:12] Sofia Ramos: One more: model governance. We need to pin model versions and be able to rollback.
[06:18] Maya Chen: Redwood offers model version pinning and rollout policies like canary and A/B with automatic fallback. We'll show the console flow.
[06:26] Liam O'Connor: Any known competitor differentiators we should consider?
[06:29] Maya Chen: Some providers lock you into their models; our differentiator is the unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, private plus model catalog that gives recommended quantization. Competitors like Anthropic/OpenAI have strong models but less flexibility for private deployments; Replicate helps with model packaging but not the full managed infra.
[06:47] Evan Zhao: Sounds good.
[06:49] Sofia Ramos: Ok, timeline: we have procurement windows in August; ideally a pilot in late July or early August.
[06:56] Maya Chen: We'll aim to have pricing and SOC2 docs to you by Friday. Can Aaron start the benchmark setup as soon as you share sample payloads?
[07:04] Aaron Patel: Yes, once we have samples and access requirements.
[07:08] Sofia Ramos: We'll send the dataset and example conversations by Friday.
[07:13] Liam O'Connor: Great.
[07:15] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick recap: Maya to send pricing and SLA; Aaron to share SOC2/architecture and coordinate benchmark; Nyx to share test payloads and language list. Benchmarks week of Jul 27. Anything else?
[07:27] Evan Zhao: No, that's all.
[07:29] Sofia Ramos: Thanks everyone.
[07:31] Maya Chen: Thanks, talk soon.

Note: transcription contains minor mishearings (e.g., product names) and occasional speaker label errors. Shared artifacts referenced during call: /drive/nyx/redwood-benchmark-spec.xlsx, Redwood SOC2 summary (link sent after call).
